title: benchmark-sample-sketchpad-apr07-2026
content:
Attendees: Aisha, Marco, Dana, Ravi, Ellen
Date: 2026-04-07
Location: perf-sync quick slot (standup lane)
Objective: sketch out a focused sampling experiment to reproduce the intermittent throughput gap seen on release-2026-04 when using the new q8 int8 kernels. This doc is a working pad — rough runs, logs, and hypotheses.

Quick context (TL;DR):
- Prod-like canary (release-2026-04) shows a 8-12% throughput drop at median QPS under mixed short/long seq workloads compared to release-2026-03. Tail (p99) occasionally spikes ~30% for 30–45s.
- Suspected vector: kernel change in q8 path + different batching behavior when prefix cache hit-rate dips below ~70%.
- Repro on bench cluster is flaky; need deterministic sample harness and smaller isolation toys.

What we ran today (notes):
- run id: sample-20260407-a (short-only, seq=64, batch cap=128)
  - command: ./bench --model redwood-13b-q8 --seq 64 --warmup 120 --qps 200 --batch-cap 128 --trace s3://perf-runs/sample-20260407-a.trace
  - outcome: stable qps, no throughput gap, p95 ~ 32ms
- run id: sample-20260407-b (mixed, seq dist 8/64/512 ~ 60/35/5)
  - command: ./bench --model redwood-13b-q8 --seq-mix config/mix-60-35-5.json --qps 200 --batch-cap 128 --trace s3://perf-runs/sample-20260407-b.trace
  - outcome: intermittent 9–11% throughput drop starting ~t+240s; CPU on host-3 saw short spikes; KV cache hit-rate dropped from 78% -> 58% during dip window (per trace).
- run id: sample-20260407-c (same as b but q8 disabled -> q4 fallback)
  - outcome: no drop, slightly higher token latency (p50 +4ms) but stable throughput.

Immediate observations:
- The gap correlates with two events: (1) a sequence of requests that reduces prefix cache hit-rate (many longer sequences that bypass cached prefixes), and (2) a kernel switch path in q8 where an internal loop re-allocates a small temporary buffer (seen in host logs).
- Host logs (host-3) show repeated small allocations (alloc_small_buffer()) concurrent with KV eviction bursts. These coincide with increased malloc contention in the perf VM.
- When q8 is disabled the alloc pattern is absent and throughput holds.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) q8 kernel path contains a microallocation hot path that is normally amortized by cache hits; when cache hit-rate falls the extra allocations manifest as short GC-like pauses and degrade throughput. (High confidence)
2) Batch packing heuristics in the scheduler react to reduced cache reuse by increasing per-request copying; q8 suffers more because of alignment/padding differences. (Medium)
3) Oversubscription of CPU on specific NUMA node (host-3) amplifies the pause when q8 does the microalloc. (Low-medium)

Next investigatory runs to schedule (owners assigned):
- Deterministic KV stress + single-host isolate (Marco): create a synthetic stream that intentionally warms prefix cache then flips to cold keys to force hit-rate swing. Run with q8 vs q4 and capture malloc traces. Due: 2026-04-09. Linked run prefix: kv-swing-20260409.*
- Instrument q8 kernel to avoid microallocation (Dana + Ravi): replace alloc_small_buffer() with pre-allocated thread-local scratch and run same stress. Collect traces. Due: 2026-04-10. PR sketch: github PR-1224 (WIP).
- Scheduler shadow mode (Ellen): run the scheduler with batch-packing disabled and with a conservative packing threshold to see if behavior changes. Compare p50/p95/p99 and batch-size distribution. Due: 2026-04-09.
- NUMA/placement check (Aisha): repro host-3 placement across different instance types and pin threads to isolate CPU contention. Due: 2026-04-11.

Short checklist for each run (manual):
- capture full /proc/meminfo and vmstat at 5s interval
- enable malloc tracing (jemalloc stats) for the process
- capture KV cache heatmap (kvcache/metrics at 1s)
- upload traces to s3://perf-runs/<run-id>.trace and add to linked_artifacts

Unresolved questions / open items:
- Is the alloc_small_buffer() change introduced in PR #1187 or #1219? Need code blame. (Marco)
- Can we reproduce on dedicated pools (not bench cluster) to confirm it's not an infra artifact? (Aisha)
- Does quantization variant (q5 vs q8) show same pattern? We only tried q4 fallback; need q5 run. (Dana)

Quick decisions made in sync:
- Do not roll back q8 on prod canary yet — impact is intermittent and p50 change is small; we will block rollout only if we observe >15% sustained throughput drop or persistent p99 regressions. (agreed)
- Prioritize kernel instrumentation before more large-scale perf runs.

Notes to self / heuristics:
- When debugging throughput gaps, isolate three levers: cache-hit-rate, kernel path allocation profile, scheduler packing. Try to hold two constant and vary one.
- Use small reproducible harnesses (30–60s experiments) and then scale-up if consistent.

Artifacts & pointers mentioned in meeting:
- perf traces: s3://perf-runs/sample-20260407-*.trace
- host logs: s3://hostlogs/host-3/2026-04-07/*.log
- related PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1224 (WIP)
- investigation ticket: JIRA-ENG-4812

Action owners recap:
- Marco: kv-swing synthetic stream + reproduce (due 04-09)
- Dana + Ravi: q8 microalloc instrumentation + bench runs (due 04-10)
- Ellen: scheduler shadow-run + pack-threshold sweep (due 04-09)
- Aisha: NUMA placement tests and confirm on dedicated pool (due 04-11)

Final: next sync scheduled 2026-04-09 09:30 UTC (30m). Bring traces and preliminary malloc flamegraphs.

Notes appended: this doc is a working sketch — expect updates after Marco's run and Dana's quick patch. If you copy fragments to Confluence, mark as draft.
